cards.power: PASSIVE. Automatically converts all official government narratives into comedic fodder.
cards.lore: Atlantis sank, the aliens are feds, and your tax dollars bought a secret moon base. Deal the cards!
cards.gradeReason: Instant identity: you ARE the comedic fodder machine. Zero barrier to entry.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro cartoon. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit riding rocket trash can through stars. Mood: gleefully absurd.

cards.power: INITIATIVE. He who holds the File commands the military-industrial complex.
cards.lore: Higher classification than the atomic bomb. It's not about little green men; it's about proprietary tech.
cards.gradeReason: One sentence role. Holds the file, runs the complex. Table immediately knows what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: classified document aesthetic. Subject: glowing filing cabinet above clouds, eagle-men in trenchcoats watching. Mood: paranoid.

cards.power: SURVIVAL. When the board is wiped, these guys ignore the rules and keep their wealth tokens.
cards.lore: Democracy is just the weather. COG is the climate. They survive the floods and the assassinations.
cards.gradeReason: 'Democracy is weather, COG is climate' — one of the best lore lines in the corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political thriller. Subject: walrus-men in suits playing chess on world map in stone bunker. Mood: cold, calculating.

cards.power: EXTRACTION. Siphon 2 Truth Tokens from your opponent's hand without them noticing.
cards.lore: A financial top using dirty tricks. The Deep State doesn't care who is in office, as long as the spice flows.
cards.gradeReason: EXTRACTION + 'spice flows' Dune reference. Instant character embodiment, no setup needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir watercolor. Subject: octopus puppet master controlling mouse politicians on stage under spotlight. Mood: shadowy, theatrical.

cards.power: HARMONY. Reveal the top card of the deck; if it's a weapon, turn it into a flower.
cards.lore: The original spiritual seekers of Atlantis. Wanted to commune with the saintly realms, got infiltrated by defense contractors instead.
cards.gradeReason: Beautiful concept but Cayce Amelius lore needs table context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ethereal watercolor. Subject: spiral of axolotls swimming in pink cosmic light formation. Mood: serene, ancient.

cards.power: DESTRUCTION. Sacrifice your own civilization to deal 10 damage to the board.
cards.lore: Occult evil meets defense spending. They weaponized the TUAOI stone and drowned 50,000 years of history in Meltwater Pulse 1B.
cards.gradeReason: Sacrifice your own civilization. Players immediately know how evil this role is.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark cartoon apocalypse. Subject: mutant toad-creature smashing red buttons at weapons panel, crystal glowing malevolently. Mood: chaotic.

cards.power: OVERCHARGE. Generates infinite energy, but rolls a 1-in-6 chance of causing a cataclysmic flood.
cards.lore: An Atlantean power grid tuned to the sun and stars. The ultimate clean energy tech, currently chilling at the bottom of the Bermuda Triangle.
cards.gradeReason: The 1-in-6 flood risk is immediately performable as table drama. Everyone watches the die.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sci-fi crystal art. Subject: glowing blue Atlantean crystal on pedestal with lightning arcs and ocean below. Mood: magnificent, dangerous.

cards.power: LABOR. Generates free work tokens, but slowly drains the player's Empathy stat.
cards.lore: Flesh mixed with machine to trap human souls for free labor. The original AI threat.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept but 'Empathy stat' mechanic needs game system context. Good once explained.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: steampunk sad. Subject: teddy bear with exposed gears sitting beside robot dog, both looking dejected. Mood: melancholic, eerie.

cards.power: FORESIGHT. Look at the opponent's hand. You literally lived this life 12,000 years ago.
cards.lore: Edgar Cayce's past life. Brought Atlantean records to Egypt before the water got too high.
cards.gradeReason: 'You literally lived this life 12,000 years ago' is funny but Cayce/Rata identity needs intro.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Egyptian cartoon epic. Subject: possum in pharaoh regalia with scepter leading big cats through desert. Mood: prophetic, grand.

cards.power: CONSTRUCTION. Build one indestructible structure token.
cards.lore: Initiate of the Great White Brotherhood. Laid out Giza 50,000 years ago to stash the Atlantean backups.
cards.gradeReason: Clear mechanic but 'Great White Brotherhood' and Atlantean backup concept needs table setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ancient meets futuristic. Subject: ibis-headed figure with holographic pyramid schematics in desert. Mood: architectural, cosmic.

cards.power: HOARD. Stash 5 knowledge cards under this entity. They cannot be destroyed.

cards.gradeReason: HOARD mechanic is clear. 'Good luck getting the permits' lands well. Needs Cayce intro.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: archaeological mystery. Subject: giant stone paw pressing down on wooden trapdoor in desert sand. Mood: secretive, monumental.

cards.power: BANISH. Removes one Dark Magic token from the board.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mesoamerican mythic. Subject: rainbow quetzal bird battling swirling shadow creature in jungle light. Mood: sacred combat, vibrant.

cards.power: ATAVISTIC MEDIUMSHIP. Draw 5 secret cards from the astral discard pile.

cards.gradeReason: 'She was the firehose' — instantly playable. Players know exactly who they're embodying.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: occult vintage. Subject: walrus-woman medium at typewriter with ghost smoke rising dramatically. Mood: mystical, defiant.

cards.cardName: Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn
cards.power: RITUAL. Attempt to summon an entity: 50% chance the group breaks up over petty infighting.

cards.gradeReason: The 'biggest hat' internal politics joke makes the table laugh and play immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ceremonial chaos. Subject: owl wizards in robes arguing while waving wands, ritual circle glowing behind them. Mood: pompous, comic.

cards.power: SUBTERRANEAN BOOST. Doubles the effectiveness of all underground units.
cards.lore: Bulwer-Lytton's sci-fi concept that mystery schools took way too seriously. The life force of the coming race.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: subterranean adventure. Subject: mole with goggles channeling blue lightning in underground cave. Mood: electrifying, cavernous.

cards.power: TRAP. Any unit defeated by this card cannot be returned to the deck. Lost to virtual reality.
cards.lore: Steiner's ultimate warning: a spiritual trap built of AI and materialism designed to stop human reincarnation [text truncated]
cards.gradeReason: TRAP mechanic is clear and dark. Steiner context cuts off but 'lost to virtual reality' lands.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: digital void horror. Subject: spiral vortex of screens and ghost rabbits swirling into black hole. Mood: existential dread.

cards.power: LIFE READING. Skip your turn to perfectly predict the opponent's next 3 moves.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: trance dreamscape. Subject: sloth sleeping on velvet couch, astral projection floating through galaxies above. Mood: serene, prophetic.

cards.power: GEOPOLITICAL TENSION. Play this location to force all players to discard their hands and panic.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: underwater action. Subject: pelican diver with goggles dodging sharks and explosions near submerged temple. Mood: chaotic, tropical.

cards.power: VALIDATION. Proves one of your crazy theories to be true. Gain +2 Credibility.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: underwater archaeology. Subject: crab with crown measuring stone blocks on ocean floor with measuring tape. Mood: triumphant, aquatic.

cards.power: INVISIBLE HELP. Fixes one broken item or gives you +1 Inspiration.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: garden whimsy. Subject: raccoons and cats gardening with tools, badger napping in hammock. Mood: peaceful, helpful.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: explosive rocket mysticism. Subject: coyote in lab coat with grimoire pouring chemicals amid explosion and UFOs. Mood: wild, doomed.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: desert ritual spectacle. Subject: foxes dancing around campfire with aurora sky full of UFOs and cacti. Mood: psychedelic, cosmic.

cards.power: BLACK SITE. Generate weapone without international oversight.

cards.power: THE CAT IS OUT. Forces the opposing player into a permanent state of cover-up mode.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: desert mystery. Subject: armadillo in overalls poking strange metallic debris with glowing hieroglyphics in New Mexico desert. Mood: bewildered.

cards.power: GASLIGHT. Nullifies any Truth card played against you this turn.

cards.power: INSURANCE POLICY. Keep one secret card from your hand hidden from all game effects.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: investigative drama. Subject: basset hound officer in uniform secretly pocketing debris sample from evidence table. Mood: cautious, loyal.

cards.power: COMPLETE CLASSIFICATION. You control all info. Opponents play with cards face down.

cards.gradeReason: 'Do not mess with their filing cabinets.' Players immediately know the stakes and the role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: shadow government noir. Subject: silhouetted animal figures at table with TOP SECRET stamp glowing red. Mood: ominous, powerful.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark political cartoon. Subject: deer in business suit at open window with black shadow creature, papers flying. Mood: tragic, tense.

cards.power: MANCHURIAN CANDIDATE. Take control of one of your opponent's units for one turn.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychedelic control. Subject: hyena hypnotist with pocket watch over spiral-eyed sheep in swirling colorful room. Mood: sinister, colorful.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: institutional paranoia. Subject: crow agents in suits showing confused small bird a TV screen with fake UFO footage. Mood: bureaucratic, menacing.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: presidential tragedy. Subject: lion at podium reading file with gun crosshair overlaid, cameras flashing. Mood: dramatic, ominous.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: spy operation. Subject: vultures and mouse soldier setting up box trap at Texas School Book Depository. Mood: calculating, cold.

cards.power: SIGNAL. Trigger a massive, board-altering event.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: classified futurism. Subject: sleek alien-fish spaceship hidden behind old Saturn V rocket, raccoons loading cargo. Mood: clandestine, vast.

verdict: Sixty cards of pure dark journalism kayfabe and this deck doesn't blink once — the narrative arc from Atlantis to AI Trap Door is the tightest thematic spine in the corpus, every cluster connects. Named strength: Secretary Forrestal being 'discarded out a window' is the single best dark punchline in any deck analyzed to date. Named weakness: the Atlantis/esoteric block (pages 2-3) requires 30 seconds of table setup that the Roswell/CIA block does not. Three lore lines are truncated at the card edge — minor but fixable before print. Table-ready? Yes, with prejudice.
blurb: For anyone who's ever wondered what's really in the UFO file — and who benefits. Sixty cards spanning Atlantis, Roswell, MK Ultra, and the AI Architects in one crisply argued conspiracy card game.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — FrizzleBob rocket trash can is strong character visual; 4-up cover format makes it slightly busy but energetic
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'Welcome to the Cosmic Grift!' / 'KayfaBIZARRO!' — punchy, clear, shareable
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — UFO files, deep state, Atlantis thesis matched perfectly from card one
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — classic Kayfabizarro newspaper format but with strong individual thematic identity
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — 'your tax dollars bought a secret moon base. Deal the cards!' is peak shareable copy
coverQA.coverNote: The cover card (Welcome to the Cosmic Grift!) functions as both intro and deck manifesto — rare to see that done this cleanly. The trash-can rocket FrizzleBob image sets tone immediately. If this cover doesn't sell on a Gumroad thumbnail, nothing will.

notes: 15 pages, 60 cards, 4 per page in 2x2 grid. Mixed layout styles: p1 newspaper 4-up with KayfaBIZARRO!/BLÖDSINN! stamps; p2-3 large full-bleed character cards with decorative crab/fish/lobster marginalia; p4+ Komika Axis header cards with various border stamps (BLÖDSINN!, KayfaBOGGLE!, KayfaBINGO!, HUMBUG!, FALSE). Every great cover story has a budget line, and somebody signs it.

You were handed the tidy version: a weather balloon, a lone gunman, a redacted page, a debunk that arrives suspiciously fast and tells you to move along. Atlantis is a bedtime story, Roswell is swamp gas, MK Ultra was "a few bad actors," and the men funding all of it would simply never lie to you. The official debunk is not the end of the investigation. It is the most expensive part of the production, and you are the audience it was budgeted for.

Cosmic Grift is dark journalism you play with your hands: 60 cut-and-play cards that run Atlantis, Roswell, MK Ultra, and the AI Architects through one thread, the question of who actually profits. You pick up a card, you argue the case out loud, and the table decides whether the cover story holds or gets exposed mid-sentence.
